description: VAULT-MESSAGING 0.90.3 §3.4.1 rule U and §6.2 relay_links: signed relay links. Generated by vettid-vault (vms/handshake) for the apps and service vaults to reproduce. All keys are TEST ONLY: key i is the Ed25519 key of seed 32 x (0xb0 + i). A link is {v: 1, suite: 2, old, new, sig_old, sig_new}, keys and signatures in standard base64 with padding; v and suite are not bytes of m (the label binds suite 2); m = "vettid/vms/2/relay-rotate" || old (32) || new (32) (signed_bytes_hex, one per link), sig_old = Ed25519(old, m), sig_new = Ed25519(new, m) (deterministic, RFC 8032). A chain is valid when it has 1 to 32 links, each with v 1 and suite 2, old different from new and both signatures verifying, each link's old is the previous link's new, no key appears twice, the first old is first_b64 (the deposit key) and the last new is announced_b64. An invalid case says why in reason. A form case carries its links as relay_links_json, the exact array text as a string (so that a malformed form survives this file's encoding), in place of relay_links; refusal says how: "malformed" when the strict parse of the whole message refuses it (§10.1: a member twice), "relay_unlinked" when the link is refused (vms returns the body's error with ErrRelayLink inside); every link in it is refused for its form alone: v and suite are the JSON numbers 1 and 2, no member appears twice, and keys and signatures are canonical standard base64 (padding, zero padding bits) of exactly 32 and 64 bytes.

cases.name: form_v_string
cases.reason: v is the string "1", not the number 1

cases.name: form_v_float
cases.reason: v is written 1.0, not 1

cases.name: form_duplicate_member
cases.reason: the link object has old twice (the same value)

cases.name: form_non_canonical_base64
cases.reason: old's last base64 character has non-zero padding bits (it decodes leniently to the right key)

cases.name: form_url_alphabet
cases.reason: a key or signature in the URL-safe base64 alphabet (- and _)

cases.name: form_key_31_bytes
cases.reason: old is 31 bytes

cases.name: wrong_signature
cases.reason: sig_old has its first byte XOR 0x01

cases.name: wrong_sig_new
cases.reason: sig_new has its first byte XOR 0x01 (sig_old is right)

cases.name: first_not_sender
cases.reason: first_b64 (key 2, the deposit key) is not the first link's old (key 0)

cases.name: announced_not_last
cases.reason: announced_b64 (key 1) is not the last link's new (key 2)

cases.name: identity_label
cases.reason: both signatures are over "vettid/vms/2/rotate" || old || new, the identity link's label

cases.name: old_equals_new
cases.reason: old and new are the same key (key 0), both signatures valid

cases.name: repeated_key
cases.reason: key 0 -> 1 -> 0: a key appears twice (first equals announced)

cases.name: repeated_key_later
cases.reason: key 0 -> 1 -> 2 -> 1: key 1 appears twice, not at the ends

cases.name: v_2
cases.reason: unknown v with verifying signatures: the link's v is 2; both signatures verify (v is not in m)

cases.name: suite_1
cases.reason: unknown suite with verifying signatures: the link's suite is 1; both signatures verify (the label binds suite 2)

cases.name: v_2_later_link
cases.reason: three links, the third with v 2; every signature verifies

cases.name: v_missing
cases.reason: the link has no v; both signatures verify

cases.name: suite_missing
cases.reason: the link has no suite; both signatures verify

cases.name: no_links
cases.reason: an empty array: zero links (1 to 32 are required)

cases.name: broken_chain
cases.reason: key 0 -> 1, then key 2 -> 3: the second link's old is not the first link's new

cases.name: too_many
cases.reason: 33 links, key 0 -> 1 -> ... -> 33: one more than the limit of 32
